title: producer wiring prerequisites: bounded integrity refresh, active-segment exposure, process-private pages (PAPER / shadow only)

AI-SCAN-03.refresh_rule: set to the accepted merge SHA before freeze or implementation; never pin a superseded review head (R8)

AI-SCAN-03A.refresh_rule: set to the accepted merge SHA before freeze or implementation; never pin a superseded review head (R8)

scope.producer_enable_requires: a separate Integration ruling after this contract is FROZEN and its implementation slice is accepted; this contract grants nothing

ledger_constants.source: ai_scan_ledger.py @ f756068 (AI-SCAN-03A); equal to contracts/ai_scan_03 rotation_prerequisite.limits

detects: accidental corruption (bit rot, torn writes, partial copies)
uncoordinated edits to sealed or active bytes
a stale eligibility generation after the writer stalls or dies
threat_model.does_not_detect: a local actor with write access who recomputes record_hash, segment sha256, chain and manifest_hash together; all hashes are unkeyed (keyed authentication is DEFERRED: keyed_ledger_authentication)
threat_model.readers_independent_of_eligibility: read_page re-hashes every sealed segment it reads, so a sealed edit can never reach a verified read; requirement (a) bounds how long the PRODUCER may keep appending after such an edit

refresh_cadence.problem: eligibility stays True after a sealed-segment edit until the next refresh(); append() never re-verifies sealed files; the AI-SCAN-03A refresh() re-reads every sealed byte (up to 64 GiB) and runs after every seal
refresh_cadence.thread: writer thread only; never the trading thread
refresh_cadence.tick_basis: same 60 s schedule as the AI-SCAN-03 C1 heartbeat, so one writer timer drives both
per_tick: load_manifest and require manifest_hash equal to the writer's in-memory manifest_hash (at most MAX_SEGMENTS entries)
verify the next sealed_segments_per_tick sealed entries at the rolling cursor with _read_entry (bytes, sha256, rows, no malformed line); the cursor wraps to segment 1
verify the active segment against the in-memory running digest (requirement b)
on success publish a new eligibility generation stamped with time.monotonic(); on any mismatch disable the producer (manifest_invalid or active_corrupt) and publish ineligible
refresh_cadence.sweep_basis: ceil(MAX_SEGMENTS / sealed_segments_per_tick) * tick_period_s = 1024 * 60 s = 61440 s (about 17.1 h) at the 4096-segment cap; at 100 sealed segments the sweep is 25 ticks (25 min)
refresh_cadence.seal_refresh: after a seal, verify only the manifest_hash and the newly sealed entry (at most SEG_MAX bytes); never the whole corpus
refresh_cadence.startup: full verification of every sealed segment (the existing restart index) once per writer start; see open_questions Q1
refresh_cadence.overrun: ticks never overlap; a tick still running when the next is due skips that slot (counted refresh_overrun)
refresh_cadence.eligibility_age_rule: the hook treats a generation older than eligibility_max_age_s (3 ticks) by time.monotonic() as ineligible (counted eligibility_stale): one cached tuple read plus one monotonic clock read, no disk I/O, hashing or manifest traversal (G4 unchanged)

active_segment.problem: the active segment is not hash-bound: a same-size edit to already-written rows is undetected until it is sealed, and seal() would then bind the edited bytes into the manifest
active_segment.running_digest: the writer keeps an in-memory sha256 state and byte length over exactly the bytes it appended (including any torn-line closing newline) since the active segment was opened
active_segment.digest_check: every refresh tick re-reads the active file (at most segment_bound bytes) and requires length and sha256 equal to the running digest
active_segment.pre_seal_check: _rotate / seal compares the file bytes with the running digest before hashing them into a manifest entry; a mismatch refuses the seal and disables (active_corrupt)
active_segment.max_active_bytes: segment_bound (a plain int in [SEG_MIN, SEG_MAX]); unchanged AI-SCAN-03A rotation
active_segment.forced_seal: the writer seals the active segment when the next row would exceed max_active_bytes, when it holds max_active_rows rows, or at the first tick at which it is older than max_active_age_s (counted forced_seals)
active_segment.exposure_basis: with the writer alive an active edit is detected within one tick; at most max_active_rows rows / max_active_age_s / SEG_MAX bytes are ever unbound at once, which is also the most a quarantine can drop
active_segment.manifest_lifetime_basis: age-only seals every 6 h fill 4096 segments in 4096 * 6 h = 1024 days (about 2.8 years) before manifest_full
active_segment.startup_seal: the running digest does not survive a restart, so a non-empty active segment found at writer start is parsed (every line a valid record) and sealed BEFORE the first append; a parse failure goes to recovery

recovery.action: disable the producer (active_corrupt), publish ineligible; append and seal are refused
write the manifest disable marker active_corrupt atomically so a restart stays disabled
open a durable coverage gap from the last sealed end through the detection time; any window crossing it is ineligible (G2)
at the next writer start, rename the active file to seg-NNNNNN.jsonl.quarantine-<UTC>; never deleted, never truncated, never sealed, never read as data; valid prefix rows are not re-imported
open a fresh empty active segment with the same number n and clear the marker only after a full startup verification passes
at most max_auto_recoveries per recovery_window_s; a further active_corrupt keeps the producer disabled until a separate Integration ruling

active_segment.torn_tail: a torn final line is treated as corruption: no salvage, same recovery steps

page_privacy.problem: fold_pages trusts the page dicts returned by read_page; a page that crossed a process or serialization boundary could be forged
rules: page dicts from read_page exist only inside one read_window / fold_pages call in one process
fold_pages consumes only a lazy generator over read_page in the same call; pages are never stored, cached, queued, pickled, JSON-serialized, logged or returned
the API / UI returns only the fold result (complete, views, error, pages); never a page object or its records
page_privacy.external_boundary_requires: a separate contract adding authenticated page contents (per-segment canonical line boundaries the receiver re-hashes against the verified manifest, or a keyed MAC) before any IPC; DEFERRED: ipc_page_transport

test_plan.name: test_refresh_tick_verifies_at_most_four_sealed_segments
test_plan.asserts: one tick reads at most sealed_segments_per_tick sealed entries (<= 64 MiB) plus the active segment; the cursor wraps

test_plan.name: test_full_sweep_covers_every_sealed_segment_within_bound
test_plan.asserts: a same-size sealed edit anywhere disables the producer within ceil(n / 4) ticks

test_plan.name: test_seal_refresh_verifies_only_the_new_entry
test_plan.asserts: a seal reads only the new segment, never the corpus

test_plan.name: test_stale_eligibility_is_refused_on_the_hot_path
test_plan.asserts: a generation older than 180 s is ineligible with no disk I/O or hashing

test_plan.name: test_active_same_size_edit_detected_within_one_tick
test_plan.asserts: the running digest catches a same-size edit (including one with a recomputed record_hash) at the next tick

test_plan.name: test_pre_seal_digest_mismatch_refuses_the_seal
test_plan.asserts: an edited active segment is never bound into the manifest

test_plan.name: test_forced_seal_at_bytes_rows_and_age
test_plan.asserts: each of the three caps seals the active segment

test_plan.name: test_startup_seals_a_nonempty_active_before_append
test_plan.asserts: the first append after a restart lands in a fresh segment

test_plan.name: test_corrupt_active_is_quarantined_never_sealed_or_deleted
test_plan.asserts: recovery steps 1-5 in order; the quarantined bytes are preserved; the span is a coverage gap

test_plan.name: test_second_corruption_in_window_stays_disabled
test_plan.asserts: a second active_corrupt within 24 h is not auto-recovered

test_plan.name: test_pages_never_leave_the_fold
test_plan.asserts: no page dict is serialized, queued, cached or returned by the API; fold_pages gets only the in-process read_page generator

test_plan.name: test_producer_stays_default_off
test_plan.asserts: nothing in the slice enables the producer or reads the flag as on

open_questions.question: startup still verifies every sealed byte (up to 64 GiB at the cap) to build the restart index; accept as a once-per-start cost, or require a bounded startup (index sidecar) before the producer is enabled?
is the unkeyed threat model acceptable for PAPER, with keyed_ledger_authentication deferred?
tick 60 s, 4 segments per tick (17.1 h worst-case sweep), active age 6 h, 10000 rows, 1 auto-recovery per 24 h: accept or retune?
